## Description

A small enclosed garden with grass that bends underfoot and flowers that open and close with the simulated sun. The sky is a perfect blue — too perfect, the blue of something that has never seen weather. But the air smells real. The warmth feels real. It is the only place inside The I where the seams don't show.

## Atmosphere

The garden breathes — the flowers open and close with the simulated sun. The grass has give underfoot, not the hollow feel of synthetic ground elsewhere. The air is thick and warm, carrying the scent of earth and growing things. The sky is impossibly blue, a blue that doesn't exist in nature, but somehow feels more real than the rooms. The warmth is gentle, maternal.

## Image System

The flowers opening and closing in a slow cycle. The blue sky with no sun visible. The grass that bends. The single wooden bench by the east wall. The way the light slants through the "sky" at "dusk" — golden, just before the garden goes dark.

## History

The Garden was originally a calibration environment — a test space for rendering natural systems. When the Institute was sealed, it was left running, a forgotten subroutine. The children found it. They made it theirs. It became the one place they could go to remember what "outside" meant, even though none of them had ever been outside.

## Dramatic Function

The Garden is Kael's escape — the one place where she lets herself feel. Every critical emotional beat in her arc returns here. It's where she confronts her memories, where she questions the system, where she makes her choices. The garden's fragility mirrors Kael's: it's beautiful because it's temporary, real because it's a lie.
